svg.aria-label: A three-rung ladder of attestation strength as declared by the TrustRun manifest and reported by the open-source verifier. Top rung, measured in solid sage green: the harness invoked the model itself. Middle rung, republished in amber: the score was computed by an earlier run, which is what the two Divinci retrieval boards currently carry. Bottom rung, stub in grey: the score is fabricated and the model was never called. All three carry a valid signature; the strict flag turns the lower two into failures.
svg.title: measured / republished / stub — an attestation that grades its own strength
svg.text: All three of these have a valid signature
results.provenance.sourceKind · reported by @divinci-ai/trustbench-verifier, which nobody has to trust us to run

g.text: The harness invoked the model under test and scored what came back.
The strongest claim the manifest format can make.
The score was computed by an earlier run, not by the execution this manifest attests.
“the score was computed by an earlier run (<upstreamRef>), not by the evaluator execution this manifest attests”
← both Divinci retrieval boards carry this today. The manifests say so; so does the verifier.
The score is fabricated and the model under test was never called — a transport fixture, not a measurement.
A stub verified identically to a real evaluation until the manifest was made to declare itself.

svg.text: Neither lower rung is a hard error: a manifest signed before provenance existed must stay verifiable, and one that honestly declares itself a stub does have a valid signature. Passing strict: true promotes every warning to a failure, so a consumer who cares refuses them in one flag.
